newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Ecuador may sign oil pipeline finance this week.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador may sign oil pipeline finance this week.

text.p: Ecuador is expected to sign a $121 million oil pipeline financing agreement with five foreign oil companies this week, industry sources in Quito said on Monday.

Occidental, Oryx, City Investing, ARCO and YPF are in the final stages of negotiation of the plan to increase capacity of Ecuador's main SOTE pipeline from 320,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 410,000 bpd.

The long-awaited work is expected to take about 10 months, and state-run Petroecuador is waiting on the financing before issuing contracts to build new tank capacity, new pipeline pumps and a loading buoy at the Pacific port of Balao.
"The talks about financing the SOTE expansion are in a very advanced stage and it is likely they will sign this week... Work could start within a month," said a source close to the negotiations.

Argentina's YPF is expected to fund more than half the total sum, given that it has most to gain from the expansion plan, he added. YPF currently produces about 50,000 bpd, but could lift this to 80,000 bpd by the end of the year if pipeline capacity were available.
The other shareholders have more or less advanced exploration, development and production plans in the country and would also benefit from more transport capacity.
Companies say the extra 80,000 bpd capacity created by the expansion would be filled immediately it became available.
The companies are putting up the finance in the form of advance tariffs for using the line, and are expected to set up a special committee to oversee the project.
